name: cyber-aware-creations
description: Eleven NIST-aligned skills for security leaders, running locally against your own files. Nine own data and persist it: risk-register scores and tracks a cybersecurity risk register with change history and board dashboards; nist-csf assesses your programme against NIST CSF 2.0 as a tracked Organizational Profile with gap analysis, coverage reporting and read-only crosswalks to ISO 27001, CIS Controls and 800-53; metrics-register trends security metrics and KRIs with direction-aware thresholds; exceptions-register runs the lifecycle of accepted risks and control exceptions and exports the evidence artifact an auditor asks for; incident-materiality structures an SEC Item 1.05 and DORA disclosure determination and its clocks, and never emits a verdict; business-context records the organisation's own facts — revenue base, crown jewels, board-voiced tolerance — and the applicability profile that narrows what a consuming skill asks — every register reads it — risk, posture, metrics, exceptions and incident. vendor-register keeps third-party arrangements with a criticality derived by tracing what each one supports back to a business workflow and confirmed by a named person, and emits no vendor score. ai-register keeps a security inventory of the AI the organisation runs — risk lives in the deployment, not the model — deriving what each deployment is exposed to under the NIST adversarial machine learning taxonomy from its recorded attributes, recording controls with evidence and a date, and never marking an attack class handled, because those mitigations are empirical and published defences have repeatedly been broken. attention-surface is the weekly counterpart to board-pack: it reads the escalations every producer already computes, groups them by decision rather than by producer, orders them without a score, and shows what changed since the last review — owning no data, muting nothing, and reporting a register it could not read as unread rather than as clean. ciso-board-translation owns the board-facing language they all call, with sourced regulatory receipts. board-pack assembles the quarterly pack as a print-ready document and an editable PowerPoint deck, and owns no data at all.

interface.longDescription: Eleven composable skills for the people accountable for security, running locally against your own files. Keep a NIST-aligned risk register with NISTIR 8286 event statements, deterministic Likelihood x Impact scoring, SP 800-30 banding, risk-appetite flagging and an append-only change log (risk-register). Track your programme against NIST CSF 2.0 as an Organizational Profile with computed gap analysis, coverage rollups and crosswalk lenses onto ISO 27001, CIS Controls and 800-53 (nist-csf). Trend metrics and KRIs with direction-aware thresholds (metrics-register). Run accepted risks and control exceptions through a re-validation lifecycle that refuses a record with no approver or justification (exceptions-register). Structure an incident materiality determination and its SEC Item 1.05 and DORA clocks, with no score and no verdict, because that judgment is made with counsel (incident-materiality). Record the organisation's own facts and the applicability profile that narrows what a consuming skill asks, read by every register (business-context). Keep a register of third-party arrangements whose criticality is derived by tracing what each one supports back to a business workflow and then confirmed by a named person, with no vendor score anywhere in it (vendor-register). Translate any metric, risk or quarter into board-ready language with sourced regulatory receipts (ciso-board-translation). Assemble it all into a quarterly board pack and an editable PowerPoint deck (board-pack). Not affiliated with or endorsed by NIST. ai-register keeps a security inventory of the AI the organisation runs — risk lives in the deployment, not the model — deriving what each deployment is exposed to under the NIST adversarial machine learning taxonomy from its recorded attributes, recording controls with evidence and a date, and never marking an attack class handled, because those mitigations are empirical and published defences have repeatedly been broken. attention-surface is the weekly counterpart to board-pack: it reads the escalations every producer already computes, groups them by decision rather than by producer, orders them without a score, and shows what changed since the last review — owning no data, muting nothing, and reporting a register it could not read as unread rather than as clean.
